nodes.name: Melt Spinning
nodes.procedure: The Fe78Si9B13 amorphous alloy ribbons were prepared by melt spinning in a high-purity argon (99.999%) atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, the Fe78Si9B13 amorphous alloy ribbons were prepared by melt spinning in a high-purity argon (99.999%) atmosphere.

nodes.name: Cutting into Circles
nodes.procedure: The ribbons with width of 6 cm and thickness of 20 μm were cut into circle pieces with a diameter of Φ = 10 mm by a punching machine.
nodes.source_text: Secondly, the ribbons with width of 6 cm and thickness of 20 μm were cut into circle pieces with a diameter of Φ = 10 mm by a punching machine.

nodes.name: Ultrasonic Vibration 50J
nodes.procedure: 5 pieces of the punched circles were put into a Branson 2000X Ultrasonic Welding Machine for ultrasonic vibration (UV) process. The experimental parameters of UV are as follows: welding pressure of 200 kPa, trigger pressure of 200 N, vibration amplitude of 80%, holding time of 12 s, and the ultrasonic energy applied to the Fe78Si9B13 amorphous alloys are 50 J, which are marked as UV-50J.
nodes.source_text: Thirdly, 5 pieces of the punched circles were put into a Branson 2000X Ultrasonic Welding Machine for ultrasonic vibration (UV) process... ultrasonic energy applied... 50 J, which are marked as UV-50J.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show broad amorphous humps with no crystallization even at highest ultrasonic energy of 5000J.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the XRD patterns of the amorphous Fe_{78}Si_9B_{13} alloys before and after UV treatments. Even at the highest ultrasonic energy of 5000J, the amorphous alloy does not crystallize.

nodes.characterization_summary: Crystallization enthalpy (ΔHc) increases from 141.54 J/g for untreated alloy to 145.32 J/g for UV-5000J sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b shows the crystallization behavior of amorphous Fe_{78}Si_9B_{13} alloy and the UV-5000J sample. ... the enthalpy change of crystallization (ΔH_C) for the amorphous Fe_{78}Si_9B_{13} alloy is 141.54 J/g ... After UV treatment with energy of 5000J, ΔH_C is increased to 145.32 J/g

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe 2p shows Fe0 at 706.5eV & 719.1eV, Fe2+ at 710.4eV, Fe3+ at 723.9eV; Si 2p shows Si0 at 99.0eV, Si2+ at 101.9eV; B 1s shows B0 at 187.4eV, BX+ at 191.4eV. No obvious difference before/after UV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a-c, the Fe 2p (Fe0 at 706.5eV & 719.1eV, Fe2+ at 710.4eV, Fe3+ at 723.9eV), Si 2p (Si0 at 99.0eV, Si2+ at 101.9eV) and B 1s (B^0 at 187.4eV, B^{X+} at 191.4eV) curves ... there is no obvious difference in the chemical state for the ribbons alloys before and after UV

nodes.characterization_summary: Melt-spun alloy surface is flat; after UV treatment becomes fragmented with abundant cracks and glass chips; UV-5000J shows staggered micro-cracks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Microstructures of the melt-spun Fe_{78}Si_9B_{13} alloy before and after UV treatments are shown in Fig. 3. The surface of the melt-spun alloy is very flat, but it is fragmented upon high frequency vibrations ... which cause abundant cracks and glass chip.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping of glass chip from UV-5000J shows small amount of oxygen, likely trace oxide film.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3f shows the EDS mapping of a glass chip. It reveals that glass chip peeled off from the sample with the largest vibration energy, contains a small amount of oxygen

nodes.characterization_summary: After 1000 CV cycles, Fe0 peaks at 706.5eV & 719.1eV disappear indicating Fe0 consumption; Si and B elements show dealloying.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After 1000 CV, the Fe^0 peaks at 706.5eV & 719.1eV have disappeared, which indicates that Fe^0 is consumed as the main active substance in HER. ... Si elements (Si^0 at 99.0eV Si^{2+} at 101.9eV) and B elements (B^0 at 187.4.9eV and B^{X+} at 191.4eV) all have been dealloyed
